skill.name: python-web-app-security-audit
skill.description: Run defensive pre-release security tests for Python web applications. Use for FastAPI, Django, Flask, and ASGI services: the common interface between Python web apps and servers. Tests authentication, authorization, hostile input, headers, CORS, cookies, rate limits, errors, and configuration to return evidence-backed findings and clear test boundaries.
skill.summary: Test Python web application security controls with a configurable, in-process pytest suite.
skill.author: glenskii

security_audit.summary: All 126 static findings are false positives caused by defensive tests, local configuration, documentation formatting, or in-process ASGI requests. Two semantic risks remain: a destructive SQL injection payload and a registration probe that can persist a privileged account when an application is vulnerable. The suite should run only with an ephemeral application and disposable database.

remediation.issue: The SQL injection payload can execute a destructive DROP TABLE statement.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a non-destructive proof payload and require an ephemeral database before hostile-input tests run.

remediation.issue: The mass-assignment test can create a persistent privileged account.
remediation.suggestion: Use randomized test identities, verify stored privileges through a trusted path, and delete created accounts during fixture teardown.

remediation.issue: Safety requirements are documented but not enforced before state-changing tests.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit opt-in guard that confirms a disposable environment before destructive or mutating tests execute.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive SQL Injection Probe
semantic_findings.description: The login probe includes "'; DROP TABLE users;--". A vulnerable application connected to persistent data could execute this payload and destroy its users table.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destructive SQL statement is explicit and is submitted to the configured login route. Documentation limits use to test systems, but code does not enforce database isolation.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Account Creation Probe Can Persist
semantic_findings.description: The registration test submits administrator flags and permissions with a fixed account. A vulnerable application could create a privileged account, and the suite provides no cleanup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The state-changing registration request and privileged fields are explicit. The test only inspects the response and does not remove any created account.

content.user_title: Audit Python Web Applications Before Release
content.value_statement: Python web applications can ship with untested authentication, authorization, and configuration weaknesses. This skill provides configurable pytest checks and structured release evidence.
actual_capabilities: Copies a configurable pytest security suite into a target project without overwriting an existing security directory.
Loads a configured ASGI application and tests it without opening a public server.
Checks authentication, authorization, hostile input, headers, CORS, cookies, rate limits, errors, and configuration.
Supports route, account, origin, and rate-limit settings through a dedicated test environment file.
Provides a report template and release decision guide for evidence-backed findings.
limitations: It does not test deployment TLS, reverse proxies, WAF controls, dependencies, or cloud infrastructure.
Flask applications require a maintained ASGI adapter before testing.
Results depend on accurate route settings and isolated test accounts.
Several probes mutate application state or send destructive input, so an ephemeral test database is required.

use_cases.title: Pre-release API review
use_cases.description: Run focused security checks against configured routes before approving a Python API release.

use_cases.title: Framework control verification
use_cases.description: Verify authentication, CORS, cookies, headers, and validation behavior across an ASGI application.

use_cases.title: Release evidence preparation
use_cases.description: Document failures, skipped checks, test boundaries, remediation, and a release decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review test readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Python web application and identify the routes, test accounts, origins, and limits needed to configure this security suite.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare the suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the bundled security suite for [project path], preserve existing files, and explain every configuration value that still needs input.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze test failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the configured security tests, separate confirmed weaknesses from setup errors, and report evidence, severity, remediation, and untested boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a release decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess the security results for revision [revision], correlate related failures, challenge false positives, and produce a defensible release decision with retest criteria.

output_examples.input: Assess an API where the protected profile route returns success without a token.
output: Finding: The profile route permits unauthenticated access.
Severity: High because account data may be exposed.
Recommendation: Enforce authentication middleware and retest anonymous, invalid-token, and valid-token requests.

output_examples.input: Interpret a failed test that used the default admin route, but the application has no admin endpoint.
output_examples.output: Configuration issue, not a vulnerability. Mark the check as not applicable, record the missing control, and do not block release from this result.

output_examples.input: Summarize a run with resolved header failures and an untested external identity provider.
output_examples.output: Review required. Header findings passed retesting, but identity-provider behavior remains outside the configured suite and needs separate evidence.

best_practices: Run the suite only against an isolated application instance with disposable data and dedicated test accounts.
Configure every route and threshold before interpreting failures as security defects.
Record skipped checks, environmental boundaries, remediation, and retest evidence with the release decision.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive probes against production data or public endpoints.
Do not treat framework defaults or example routes as evidence about the application.
Do not present a passing suite as a penetration test or proof of complete security.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: FastAPI and Django ASGI applications work directly. Flask requires a maintained ASGI adapter.

faq.question: Does the suite open a network server?
faq.answer: No. The HTTP client uses an in-process ASGI transport with a test base URL.

faq.question: Can I run it against production?
faq.answer: No. Use an isolated instance, disposable database, and dedicated accounts because several checks send hostile or state-changing requests.

faq.question: Does a passing run prove the application is secure?
faq.answer: No. It only covers the configured application, routes, accounts, and controls reachable through ASGI.

faq.question: Does it test infrastructure and dependencies?
faq.answer: No. Review TLS, proxies, WAF controls, cloud settings, dependencies, and external identity providers separately.

faq.question: How should skipped tests affect release decisions?
faq.answer: A skipped test is not a pass. Record why it was skipped and provide separate evidence for the relevant control.
